Curriculum for Endoscopic Treatment of Esophageal Neoplasia and Precursor Lesions: ESGE Position Statement – with Competency Assessment Tools
  • Source: Endoscopy, Vol. 58, Issue 2026 (published online 2026-09-24)
  • Topic: Training curriculum for endoscopic therapy of esophageal neoplasia and precursor lesions
  • Author(s): Weusten BLAM, Pouw RE, Bergman JJ, et al. (26 authors total)
1. Overview and Scope
  • ESGE official statement on training for endoscopic therapy of early esophageal cancer and precursor lesions
  • Covers both Barrett esophagus-related neoplasia (BERN) and esophageal squamous cell neoplasia (ESCN)
  • Aims to help endoscopists improve skills in endoscopic therapy for precancerous lesions and early esophageal cancer
  • Sets prerequisites for trainee's and trainer's working environments
2. Pre-Training Knowledge Requirements
  • Trainee must be aware of different treatment modalities and their specific indications and limitations for esophageal neoplasia and precursor lesions
  • Level of agreement: 100%
2.1 Key Documents to Study
  • Optical diagnosis of esophageal lesions
  • Indications for different endoscopic treatment options
  • General principles of EMR, ESD, and ablation including:
  • Different tools (cap-based devices, snares, knives, coagulation forceps, RFA devices, APC and cryoballoon ablation tools)
  • Understanding of electrosurgical unit settings
  • Prevention and management of complications (bleeding, perforation, strictures)
  • Consequences of histopathology results ("curative" vs "noncurative" resections) per current guidelines
  • Management of advanced disease not amenable to endoscopic treatment (surgery, chemotherapy/radiotherapy, neoadjuvant/adjuvant concepts)
2.2 Recommended Pre-Training Activity
  • Participation in regular multidisciplinary tumor board meetings during pre-training or early training phase
3. Pre-Training Skills Requirements
  • Proficiency in management of adverse events (bleeding, perforation, strictures) is mandatory before starting esophageal cancer treatment curriculum
  • Level of agreement: 94%
3.1 Minimum Experience Thresholds
  • Suggested minimum before starting esophageal neoplasia training:
  • ≥4 years of endoscopy practice
  • ≥1000 endoscopic procedures performed
3.2 Diagnostic EGD Competency Benchmarks
  • Scope-tip control competency (score >3.5/4.0) achieved after 350 EGDs
  • Global competency in diagnostic EGD (3 domains: pre-procedure skills, technical skills, post-procedure nontechnical skills) achieved after 225–249 procedures
  • Rate of intubation to second part of duodenum and J-maneuver in ≥95% of procedures required for accreditation
3.3 Interval Cancer Correlation
  • Interval esophageal cancers strongly associated with:
  • <5 years' practice experience
  • <1000 EGD procedures performed
4. Thresholds for Competency
4.1 General Requirements
  • Optical diagnosis competency is a prerequisite to achieve proficiency in endoscopic management of early esophageal neoplasia
  • Level of agreement: 100%
  • Proficiency in both endoscopic resection AND ablation is mandatory for competency in early Barrett neoplasia management
  • Level of agreement: 96%
4.2 Barrett Esophagus-Related Neoplasia (BERN) Thresholds
  • Complete eradication of intestinal metaplasia (CEIM): >80%
  • Complete eradication of neoplasia (CEN): >90%
  • Treatment completion within 18 months
  • Perforation rate maintained at <1% --> indicator of safe treatment
  • These thresholds can be considered indicators of competency in providing effective and safe BE-related neoplasia treatment
  • Level of agreement: 94%
4.2.1 BERN Treatment Outcomes
  • Median RFA sessions to achieve CEIM: 2–3 (range 1–5) in expert hands
  • Treatment cessations due to "failure" occur within 18 months (median 8 months)
  • Recurrence of dysplasia: ~1% per year in expert setting
  • Esophageal adenocarcinoma not amenable to endoscopic therapy: only 0.1% per year over median follow-up of 43 months
4.2.2 BERN Treatment Strategy
  • Multimodal approach: endoscopic resection for all visible lesions + RFA for flat segments ± APC for smaller areas
  • EMR of visible neoplastic BE lesions precedes RFA in >50% of patients (Dutch nationwide cohort, n=1386)
  • Additional endoscopic resection needed in ~5% of patients during ablation phase for newly detected lesions
  • Multiband EMR or cap-assisted EMR are equally effective --> either technique acceptable
4.2.3 ESD Indications in BERN
  • Certain lesions require ESD (not just EMR)
  • Endoscopists should be familiar with specific ESD indications for BERN
  • Proficiency in EMR is a prerequisite
  • Proficiency in ESD is desirable but not mandatory
  • If lacking ESD proficiency, established collaboration with recognized ESD center is necessary
4.2.4 EMR-Only Strategy
  • May be valid alternative for patients of advanced age or with comorbidities unlikely to benefit from secondary prevention with ablation
  • May also be preferred for rare cases where reaching CEIM is unrealistic (e.g., very long BE segments with cylindrical epithelium regeneration)
4.3 Esophageal Squamous Cell Neoplasia (ESCN) Thresholds
  • ESD is treatment of choice for most superficial esophageal squamous cell lesions
  • En bloc resection rate: >90%
  • R0 resection rate: >85%
  • Perforation rate: <3%
  • Need for urgent surgery: <1% --> can be considered indicators of competency
  • Level of agreement: 96%
4.3.1 ESCN Ablation Contraindication
  • Working group recommends against endoscopic ablation for ESCN due to:
  • Risk of "hidden" recurrences
  • Lack of adequate specimen for histopathology
4.3.2 ESCN ESD Learning Curve
  • Minimum of 30 ESD cases for esophageal neoplasia needed to achieve early proficiency
  • En bloc and R0 resection rates increase with ESD volume over time
  • Ability to manage challenging lesions (left lateral localization, size >3cm, ≥half circumference) increases with expertise
  • Time for dissection per square centimeter is inversely proportional to number of cases performed
5. Training Program Structure
5.1 Endoscopic Resection Training
  • Should be learned through structured training program consisting of:
  • Lectures
  • Live demonstrations
  • Hands-on training on models
  • Followed by training in humans under strict expert supervision (hands-on setting)
  • Minimum of 10 supervised cases on ex vivo/in vivo models recommended
  • Level of agreement: 100%
5.1.1 EMR Training Requirements
  • ≥30 resections required to achieve proficiency in esophageal EMR:
  • 10 might be carried out in models
  • 10 should be done under direct expert supervision (hands-on setting)
  • Remaining 10: alternative supervision strategies acceptable (e.g., supervision of integral videorecorded cases, remote video connection)
  • Level of agreement: 88%
5.1.2 ESD Training Requirements
  • ≥20 ESD procedures in animal models before human practice
  • Goal: at least 8 en bloc complete resections in last 10 training cases with no perforation
  • First 10 procedures in humans should be done under supervision of ESD-proficient endoscopist
  • (Derived from ESGE curriculum for ESD [19])
5.1.3 EMR Training Program Outcomes
  • Structured training implementation in Netherlands resulted in 92.5% resection rate by trainee endoscopists
  • First 20 esophageal endoscopic resections associated with 5% perforation rate (using ER-cap lift-and-snare technique)
  • Current multiband mucosectomy technique associated with perforation rate <1%
5.2 Endoscopic Ablation Training Requirements
  • 10 supervised cases of RFA (5 balloon-based + 5 focal ablation procedures) sufficient to achieve proficiency IF trainee already reached proficiency in:
  • Optical diagnosis
  • Endoscopic resection
  • Insufficient evidence about learning curve for other ablation techniques
  • Level of agreement: 96%
5.3 Training Registry Requirements
  • Endoscopists should establish prospective registry of cases to evaluate progress of esophageal endoscopic resection training
  • Registry should include:
  • En bloc resection rate
  • R0 resection rate
  • Complications
  • Procedural time
  • Final histology results
  • Technique used
  • Lesion size
  • Location
  • Endoscopic classification
  • Level of agreement: 100%
6. Maintenance of Competence Requirements
  • Annual caseload of at least:
  • 10 new cases per endoscopist with esophageal endoscopic resection
  • 10 new cases per endoscopist with endoscopic ablation --> required to maintain competence
  • Level of agreement: 94%
6.1 Volume-Outcomes Relationship
  • Higher annual caseload (30–40 RFA cases) associated with:
  • Improved CEIM and CEN rates
  • Fewer RFA sessions until CEIM
  • Lower number of rescue EMRs needed
  • ESD: >20 ESDs per year associated with acceptable results (German registry data)
  • ESGE recommends 25 ESD procedures per endoscopist per year for maintenance
6.2 Center Volume Considerations
  • Lower hospital volume (<18 ESDs per year) associated with:
  • ↑ occurrence of complications
  • ↑ perforation rates
  • ↑ in-hospital deaths
  • ↑ need for blood transfusion within 1 week after esophageal ESD
7. Trainer Center Prerequisites
  • Level of agreement: 96%
7.1 Equipment and Technical Proficiency
  • Availability of and proficiency in all endoscopic diagnostic modalities for early esophageal cancer:
  • (Virtual) chromoendoscopy
  • Zoom or near-focus high-resolution endoscopy
  • Availability of and proficiency in therapeutic modalities:
  • EMR
  • ESD
  • Endoscopic ablation techniques
7.2 Caseload Requirements
  • Sufficient caseload to:
  • Maintain proficiency of the trainer endoscopist
  • Teach to the trainee
7.3 Support Services Required
  • Dedicated pathologist with expertise in histopathology of biopsies and endoscopic resection specimens of early esophageal neoplasia
  • Access to:
  • Interventional radiology
  • Esophageal surgery
  • ICU care
7.4 Multidisciplinary Requirements
  • Availability of multidisciplinary tumor board containing expertise in:
  • Esophageal surgery
  • Medical oncology
  • Radiotherapy
  • Radiology
  • Pathology
7.5 Quality Assurance
  • Prospective registration of all cases of early esophageal cancer managed endoscopically
8. Trainee Center Prerequisites
  • Level of agreement: 96%
8.1 Equipment Requirements
  • High-resolution endoscopy equipment with:
  • Zoom or near-focus modality
  • (Virtual) chromoendoscopy
  • Equipment for both endoscopic resection and ablation in the esophagus
8.2 Anesthesia Support
  • Possibility to perform endoscopic procedures under:
  • Deep sedation
  • General anesthesia
8.3 Support Services Required
  • Access to:
  • Dedicated pathologist with expertise in early esophageal neoplasia histopathology
  • Possibility to admit patients to ward
  • Interventional radiology
  • Esophageal surgery
  • ICU care
8.4 Multidisciplinary Requirements
  • Access to multidisciplinary tumor board with expertise in:
  • Esophageal surgery
  • Medical oncology
  • Radiology
  • Radiotherapy
  • Pathology
8.5 Partnership Requirements
  • Agreement with trainer's center for management of complicated cases
8.6 Quality Assurance
  • Prospective registration of all cases of early esophageal cancer managed endoscopically
9. Available Training Resources
  • BEST-Academia (https://BEST-academia.eu)
  • Freely accessible web-based training platform
  • Designed to teach endoscopists safe and justified endoscopic treatment for BE patients
  • Contains information on imaging, treatment, and pathology
  • Specific webpages for:
  • Endoscopic resection
  • RFA
  • Cryoballoon ablation
  • Contains slideshow presentations, videos, and case discussions
9.1 BORN Module
  • Barrett's Oesophagus-Related Neoplasia training module
  • Focus on endoscopic recognition and delineation of early BE lesions
  • Accessible through BEST-Academia
9.2 Dutch Training Program Model
  • Based on Netherlands situation (BE care in 9 expert centers only)
  • Components:
  • Study of literature
  • BORN module completion (endoscopic recognition and delineation)
  • Hands-on training for endoscopic resection and RFA
  • Supervised intervision of integrally videorecorded procedures by trainees
  • Can serve as blueprint for other centers or societies
10. Competency Assessment Tools (CAT)
  • E-EMR-CAT: Endoscopic Mucosal Resection Competency Assessment Tool
  • For esophageal EMR procedures
  • E-RFA-CAT: Radiofrequency Ablation Competency Assessment Tool
  • For esophageal RFA procedures
  • Available in Supplementary Material
11. Key Statistics and Outcomes from Supporting Studies
11.1 Dutch National Database (10-year period)
  • CEIM rates: >80%
  • CEN rates: >90%
  • Perforation rate: <1% --> maintained across expert centers
11.2 UK RFA Registry Analysis
  • EMR for visible lesions prior to RFA increased significantly over time
  • Need for rescue EMR after RFA decreased from 13% to 2% with increased pre-RFA EMR
  • Improved outcomes correlated with ↑ in earlier time period to later
11.3 ESD Learning Curve Data
  • En bloc resection rate rises from 70% to 90% over first 30 procedures
  • Plateau reached after ~30 cases in supervised training setting
  • Optimal dissection speed achieved only after ~250 cases (single Western endoscopist, untutored)
11.4 RFA Learning Curve Data
  • Stable CEIM rate achieved after ~30 cases by single operator (US registry)
  • UK registry suggests 18 supervised cases may be required
  • No learning curve evident for experienced single operator (70 patients over 30 months) regarding:
  • Procedure time
  • Complications
  • Therapeutic outcomes
11.5 Animal Model Training Validation
  • Porcine model similarity to humans ranked:
  • Esophageal EMR: median score 9.0 (IQR 8.0–9.0) on scale 1–10
  • Esophageal ESD: median score 8.5 (IQR 8.0–9.0) on scale 1–10
  • Training tool usefulness scores:
  • How procedures performed: median 9.0 (IQR 7.0–10.0)
  • Usefulness for beginners: median 9.0–9.5 (IQR 8.0–10.0)
  • Animal model training as prerequisite: median 9.0–10.0 (IQR 5.0–10.0)
12. ESGE Good Practice Statements Summary
Statement Description
1 Trainee awareness of treatment modalities and indications/limitations
2 Proficiency in adverse event management (bleeding, perforation, strictures) mandatory
3 Optical diagnosis competency is prerequisite for endoscopic management proficiency
4 Both resection AND ablation proficiency mandatory for Barrett neoplasia competency
5 CEIM >80%, CEN >90% within 18 months, perforation <1% as competency indicators
6 ESD: en bloc >90%, R0 >85%, perforation <3%, urgent surgery <1% as competency indicators
7 Structured training: lectures + live demos + models → supervised human cases (min 10 on models)
8 ≥30 EMR resections needed (10 in models, 10 direct supervision, 10 alternative)
9 ≥20 ESD animal procedures before humans; ≥8 en bloc complete resections in last 10 training cases
10 First 10 human ESD procedures supervised by ESD-proficient endoscopist
11 Prospective registry with performance indicators required
12 10 supervised RFA cases (5 balloon + 5 focal) sufficient if proficient in optical diagnosis and resection
13 ≥10 new esophageal ER cases AND ≥10 new ablation cases per year to maintain competence
14 Trainer center prerequisites (7 requirements)
15 Trainee center prerequisites (8 requirements)
13. Gaps and Future Directions
  • Dedicated comprehensive training programs for ESCN do not exist --> development strongly encouraged
  • Most existing courses are single unit/center-based or industry-sponsored
  • Most focus on either endoscopic resection OR ablation, not both
  • Most consider only BE, not combination of BE and ESCN
  • Training in ablation ONLY without endoscopic resection training should be avoided by all means
